root_cause.text: The NFC digital driver's `digital_in_recv_sdd_res()` function lacks a bounds check on the accumulated `nfcid1_len` before appending bytes from each cascade round, allowing a malicious peer to trigger a heap buffer overflow by continuing the anti-collision cascade beyond the maximum three levels.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message explicitly state that "nothing in the driver actually enforces this" and that "a malicious peer can keep the cascade running, writing past the heap-allocated nfc_target with each round". The patch adds the check `if (target->nfcid1_len + size > NFC_NFCID1_MAXSIZE)` to reject oversized responses.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The NFC digital driver's `digital_in_recv_sdd_res()` function lacks a bounds check on the accumulated `nfcid1_len` before appending bytes from each cascade round, allowing a malicious peer to trigger a heap buffer overflow by continuing the anti-collision cascade beyond the maximum three levels.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE description and commit message explicitly state that "nothing in the driver actually enforces this" and that "a malicious peer can keep the cascade running, writing past the heap-allocated nfc_target with each round". The patch adds the check `if (target->nfcid1_len + size > NFC_NFCID1_MAXSIZE)` to reject oversized responses.

candidates.rationale: Sets the copy size to a fixed 4 bytes without validating that the cumulative nfcid1_len does not exceed the buffer capacity, enabling overflow when cascade rounds are repeated beyond the allowed limit.
Closes the else branch that executes the memcpy, but does not contain any bounds check; its presence as part of the vulnerable code path allows the unchecked copy to proceed.
Performs the heap buffer copy using an unchecked destination offset, directly causing an overflow if nfcid1_len has been increased beyond the allocated buffer size by prior cascade rounds.
Supplies the size argument (4 bytes) to the memcpy call; the lack of a prior bounds check on the cumulative length makes this fixed-size copy unsafe and triggerable multiple times.

Increments the length counter without verifying that the new total fits within the allocated buffer, allowing a malicious peer to artificially increase the length and cause subsequent writes to overflow.

vuln_statements.explanation: Performs the heap buffer copy using an unchecked destination offset (target->nfcid1 + target->nfcid1_len). Since nfcid1_len can be artificially increased by multiple cascade rounds without bounds checking, this memcpy can write beyond the allocated buffer, causing a heap buffer overflow.

Supplies the fixed copy size (4 bytes) to the memcpy. Without a prior bounds check on the cumulative nfcid1_len, this size remains unsafe when the cascade repeats more than three times, allowing the overflow to proceed.

Increments the length counter without verifying that the new total (nfcid1_len + size) does not exceed the allocated buffer capacity. This allows a malicious peer to artificially increase the length beyond the allowed limit, enabling subsequent copies to overflow.

Sets the copy size to a fixed 4 bytes without validating that the cumulative nfcid1_len does not exceed the buffer capacity. This fixed size, when repeatedly appended in cascade rounds beyond the maximum three levels, contributes to the heap buffer overflow.

Closes the else branch that contains the vulnerable memcpy and size increment. Its presence as part of the code path allows the unchecked copy to be executed repeatedly without any intervening bounds check, enabling the overflow.

bic_trace_step.reason: The `digital_in_recv_sdd_res()` function (lines 126-177 in diff) copies `sdd_res->nfcid1` data into `target->nfcid1` using `memcpy(target->nfcid1 + target->nfcid1_len, ...)` and increments `target->nfcid1_len` without checking that the total length does not exceed the fixed-size buffer.
